intro: Competitions, results, injuries and the language of the sports pages.
p.campeonato.consejo: It comes from «campeón». There are championships of football, chess, swimming…
p.liga.consejo: The g is hard, as in «gato»: LI-ga. The cup, by contrast, is a knockout competition.
p.eliminatoria.consejo: It comes from «eliminar». In a knockout there is a winner and an eliminated side.
p.clasificarse.consejo: You say «clasificarse para la final». It takes «se»: «el equipo se clasificó».
p.empate.consejo: The verb is «empatar». «Un empate a cero» is 0-0.
p.victoria.consejo: The stress is on «TO»: bik-TO-rya. The opposite is «la derrota».
p.derrota.consejo: The rr is strong: de-RRO-ta. «Sufrir una derrota» is to lose.
p.vencer.consejo: The c becomes z before o: «venzo». You say «vencer a un rival».
p.lesión.consejo: The verb is «lesionarse»: «se lesionó el tobillo». It has an accent: le-SIÓN.
p.aficionado.consejo: With «a» it is a fan: «aficionado al fútbol». After a noun it is amateur: «pintor aficionado».
p.medalla.consejo: The ll sounds like y: me-DA-ya. There are gold, silver and bronze medals.
p.batir.consejo: You beat a record. It also means to whisk: «batir huevos».
p.árbitro.consejo: It has an accent: ÁR-bi-tro. In football he is also called «el colegiado».
b1.texto:
**Competitions.** The **liga** lasts the whole season; the cup is a knockout. A **campeonato** has rounds: in each **eliminatoria** one loses and is out. The team that wins **se clasifica** (qualifies) for the next.

**Results.** You can win, lose or draw. The nouns are **victoria**, **derrota** and **empate**. Newspapers say **vencer** a rival.

**Prizes.** To finish champion or runner-up, win a **medalla** of gold, silver or bronze, **batir** a record, stand on the podium.

**People.** The **entrenador**, the **árbitro**, the captain, the rival and the **aficionados**.

**The body.** You train and warm up. When an athlete suffers a **lesión**, he gets injured. At the end of a career, he retires.

**Journalists' trick.** To avoid repeating, they say «el técnico» (the coach), «el colegiado» (the referee) or «el choque» (the match).
b2.f1.texto: It was a very boring draw.
b2.f2.texto: With that draw, the team can still win the league.
b2.f3.texto: First it needs a victory against its eternal rival.
b2.f4.texto: The coach says the team's star has an injury.
b2.f5.texto: The fans will not be calm until Saturday.
b2.f6.texto: If the team gets through the knockout round, it will qualify for the final.
b2.f7.texto: A defeat would be a very hard blow for everyone.
b4.texto:
**Who wins.** Use **ganar**, **perder**, **empatar** and, in newspapers, **vencer a** a rival.

**The score.** The winner takes **por** and the two numbers are joined with **a**: **ganaron por dos a uno**. A draw takes only **a**: **empataron a cero**.

**The place.** With **quedar** + place or title: **quedar tercera**, **quedar campeón**. Also: **clasificarse para** the final.
b4.e2.texto: The runner finished third in the final.
b5.f0.texto: At six in the morning, the athletics track still smells of wet grass.
b5.f1.texto: A woman of thirty-nine stretches her legs beside the starting line.
b5.f2.texto: A knee injury almost kept her away from racing two years ago.
b5.f3.texto: Every dawn she trains alone under the stars, with the cold wind on her face.
b5.f4.texto: Today, at last, she takes her place at the start and waits for the shot with her eyes closed.
b5.f5.texto: At the referee's shot, her legs set off light as birds.
b5.f6.texto: At first, the runner is last in the group and breathes with difficulty.
b5.f7.texto: Lap after lap, she overtakes all the rivals she has ahead of her.
b5.f8.texto: On the final straight, the fans cheer her on with shouts that can be heard across the whole city.
b5.f9.texto: She crosses the finish line in third place, without beating any record, and receives a bronze medal.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Training the team is the coach's job.
b6.o1.refuerzo: Tickets are sold at the box office.
b6.o2: cuida que se cumplan las reglas
b6.o2.refuerzo: Yes: the referee checks that the players follow the rules.
b6.pregunta: What does the referee do in a match?
b7.o0.refuerzo: Yes: the winning margin takes «por»: ganaron por dos a uno.
b7.o1.refuerzo: «Con» is not used for the score.
b7.o2.refuerzo: «De» is not used for the score.
b7.pregunta: Which word goes before the score?
b8.frase: El equipo se clasificó para la final
b8.traduccion: The team qualified for the final
b9.o0: un pintor que pinta muy rápido
b9.o0.refuerzo: Speed has nothing to do with «aficionado».
b9.o1: un pintor que no es profesional
b9.o1.refuerzo: Yes: after a noun, «aficionado» means he does it for pleasure.
b9.o2: un pintor al que le gusta el fútbol
b9.o2.refuerzo: That would be «aficionado al fútbol», with «a».
b11.o0.refuerzo: «Vencer» is to win; here nobody wins.
b11.o1.refuerzo: Yes: «empatar a cero» is ending goalless with no winner.
b11.o2.refuerzo: You beat a record, not a result.
b12.o0.refuerzo: Yes: breaking a record is doing it better than anyone before.
b12.o1.refuerzo: That is whisking eggs or cream. With a record, «batir» is to beat it.
b12.o2.refuerzo: A draw is not a record.
p.terminó.consejo: Past tense with the accent on NO.
p.rival.consejo: The v sounds like «b»: ri-BAL. Also works as a feminine: «la rival».
p.aficionados.consejo: From «aficionar», to attract fans. The c sounds like «s» here.
p.estarán.consejo: Future of «estar» in the plural. Stress on RAN.
p.clasificará.consejo: Future of «clasificar». In sport, «clasificarse» means to qualify.
p.duro.consejo: Stress on DU. Used as «un golpe duro», a hard blow.
p.ganó.consejo: Past of «ganar». The accent is on NO.
p.rivales.consejo: Plural of «rival». The v sounds like «b».
p.empataron.consejo: «Empatar» means to draw in sport. Stress on RON.
p.quedó.consejo: «Quedar» + position means to finish in that place.
p.pista.consejo: Feminine: «la pista». The s is clearly heard: PIS-ta.
p.atletismo.consejo: The h is silent, and the t is hard: at-le-TIS-mo.
p.rodilla.consejo: The ll sounds like «y». Feminine: «la rodilla».
p.apartó.consejo: «Apartar» means to move away. Stress on TO.
p.carreras.consejo: The rr between vowels is strong: ka-RRE-ras.
p.entrena.consejo: «Entrenar» means to train. Stress on TRE.
p.arrancan.consejo: «Arrancar» means to start moving. The rr after a vowel is strong.
p.ligeras.consejo: Feminine plural of «ligero». The g sounds like «h».
p.adelanta.consejo: «Adelantar» also means to move forward. Stress on LAN.
p.animan.consejo: «Animar» means to encourage. Stress on NI.
p.gritos.consejo: Masculine plural: «el grito». Stress on GRI.
p.oyen.consejo: «Oír» changes to «oyen» in the plural. The o starts the word.
p.meta.consejo: Feminine: «la meta». It is also a noun for goal in general.
p.cuida.consejo: «Cuidar» means to look after. «Cuidar de» is to take care of.
p.reglas.consejo: Feminine plural: «la regla». The g before l sounds hard.
p.ganaron.consejo: Past plural of «ganar». Stress on NA.
p.clasificó.consejo: Past tense of «clasificar». The accent is on KO.
p.profesional.consejo: Can also be a noun: «un profesional». Stress on NAL.
p.equipos.consejo: Masculine plural: «el equipo». Stress on KI.
p.superar.consejo: Stress is at the end: su-pe-RAR.
